title: Towards an Optimized Heterogeneous Distributed Task Scheduler in OpenMP Cluster
problem: OpenMP's shared-memory task scheduling mechanisms are inadequate for distributed cluster environments. The runtime must handle variable application balance, parallelism levels, and communication latencies in heterogeneous settings.
motivation: Improved scheduling mechanisms are critical for achieving performance and portability in distributed and heterogeneous cluster computing environments.
method: The work refactors the OMPC runtime to unify task scheduling across heterogeneous devices and hosts using the Heterogeneous Earliest Finish Time (HEFT) algorithm, which predicts finish times and assigns tasks to resources accordingly. Work Stealing and HEFT scheduling mechanisms are evaluated on real-world clusters.
key_novelty: Unified task scheduling framework across heterogeneous devices and hosts using an optimized HEFT-based algorithm for distributed OpenMP cluster environments.
contributions: Refactoring of OMPC runtime to unify task scheduling across heterogeneous devices and hosts
Optimization of HEFT-based scheduling algorithm for efficient distributed task execution
Comprehensive evaluation of Work Stealing and HEFT mechanisms in real-world cluster deployments

metrics.other: up to 24% improvement in scheduling time

limitations: The HEFT implementation in OMPC is not fully optimized and the paper does not discuss detailed application-level performance impacts or workload characteristics.
primary_theme: Distributed task scheduling for heterogeneous clusters
